title: Asymmetric routing reconciler rollout and customer escalation log
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: A subset of requests from US-west tenants intermittently routed to mismatched Dedicated pools in EU causing increased latencies, KV cache misses, and user-visible error spikes. This ticket coordinates the reconciler patch rollout, documents customer escalations and mitigation steps taken, and tracks follow-ups (observability, tests, and regressions).
root_cause_hypothesis: A transient asymmetric route advertisement at the edge (likely partial BGP flap combined with a stale router cache) caused the global traffic-router to calculate non-deterministic shortest paths. The reconciler that continuously compares edge route digests to control-plane expectations did not surface the divergence fast enough due to a sampling bug that skipped mismatched prefixes under high load.
timeline: 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC - First spike detected: 5x P95 latency increase for hosted text-gen endpoints in us-west; alert fired (latency-slo-alert).
2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Support escalations: two strategic customers (ACME Media, NovaAnalytics) opened priority tickets reporting timeouts and 5xx rates.
2026-03-10 02:26 UTC - Initial mitigation: routed 20% of us-west traffic to warm-standby region (us-east) via emergency traffic-split; latency recovered for most users.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Engineering triage: observed inconsistent route hashes between edge-proxy-1/2 and control-plane. KV cache desync metrics increased (kv-desync-rate +800%).
2026-03-10 03:15 UTC - Hotfix deployed to traffic-reconciler (v1.2.3-hotfix): sampling bug patched to include previously skipped prefixes and to add full-digest checks under elevated error rates.
2026-03-10 03:48 UTC - Phased rolling restart of regional routers with graceful connection drain started; traffic-split gradually reduced back to normal over 30 minutes.
2026-03-10 04:10 UTC - Customer comms: NOC sent interim status update to impacted customers; dedicated accounts team opened follow-up calls.
2026-03-10 05:00 UTC - Metrics stabilized; post-mitigation monitoring window started.
immediate_mitigation_steps: Apply emergency traffic-split to reroute 20-40% of impacted region traffic to warm-standby region to reduce error amplification.
Deploy reconciler sampling fix as a canary to 10% of routers, monitor route-hash-consistency and kv-desync-rate for 15 minutes.
Initiate rolling restart with graceful drain (connection drain timeout 45s) on routers where inconsistency detected.
Notify Dedicated customers with dedicated pools about potential traffic wobble and open bridge calls for highest-severity customers.
decision_log: Rollout strategy: canary reconciler -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automated health gates (route-hash-consistency > 99.9% and kv-desync-rate <= baseline * 1.2).
Rollback criteria: any sustained increase in 5xx rate above 2x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes or route-hash-consistency < 99% triggers automatic rollback and circuit-break to standby region.
Customer priority: for Dedicated customers with SLA (ACME Media, NovaAnalytics), keep traffic pinned to pre-flap routing until reconciler verifies stability for 1 hour.
rollback_plan: If the reconciler patch causes regression, revert to previous reconciler binary and immediately re-enable traffic-split to warm-standby region. Preserve current router configs and escalate to on-call infra kernel team to inspect route cache persistence. Execution owner: Marco Silva; estimated time to restore: 12-20 minutes depending on drain windows.
post_incident_followups: Add end-to-end route-hash canaries that run every 30s from multiple regions (synthetic checks).
Increase reconciler sampling coverage and introduce deterministic full-digest compare when error rates exceed threshold.
Add dashboard panels: per-tenant route-hash consistency, kv-cache-miss-by-tenant, and cross-region-traffic-split history; retention 90d.
Run tabletop with support and account teams for Dedicated customers to streamline escalation playbook and RACI.
Create automated customer-facing incident summary template and embed postmortem link in ticket close communications.

We still observed two short-lived spikes during the 2nd hour; those correlate to an unrelated control-plane deploy window and will be addressed in ENG-50500.
